title: 5 Fond du Lac County places with ghost stories to tell
excerpt: From Hotel Retlaw to Capone’s in Malone, five Fond du Lac County places have ghost stories rooted in local history and folklore.
content:
Oct. 26, 2026, 4:59 a.m. CT

  • Several historic properties in the Fond du Lac area are associated with local ghost stories and paranormal folklore.
  • Reported hauntings include changing TV channels at the Hotel Retlaw and hearing children at the Octagon House.
  • Other locations with ghostly legends are Rienzi Cemetery, Galloway House & Village, and Capone's restaurant.
  • Visitors and employees have reported phenomena such as disembodied voices, moving objects and apparitions.

FOND DU LAC – Historic properties in the Fond du Lac area have earned their share of ghost stories and folklore.

Here are some of Fond du Lac County's local legends.

Reports on Hotel Retlaw include changing TV channels, screams for help

The Hotel Retlaw, 1 N. Main St., is one of Fond du Lac's most famous sites rumored to be haunted, partly because of its age and stories about its first owner, Walter Schroeder.

Schroeder opened the hotel in 1923 and features in many of the stories of its haunting. Legend has it he wanders the halls, and prior to the hotel's 2019 renovation, tales were more widespread of him moving money around in the cash register and changing the TV channels to C-Span, according to FDL Reporter archives.

Other stories center on Room 717, with guests reporting screams for help and the door shaking among the phenomenon over the years. The stories that spread on the reasons for the hauntings include rumors of guests that have died in the hotel.

The Octagon House holds rumors of children's spirits lingering

Another well-known ghostly spot is even older than the Hotel Retlaw: the Octagon House was built on Linden Street in 1856, home to Isaac Brown and his family.

The house first opened to the public in the 1970s. Visitors could see the unique architecture and explore the secret passageways. At this time, stories of paranormal experiences surfaced. Visitors reported being shoved by an unseen force, hearing children playing and seeing the figure of Brown's daughter-in-law, Ruth Pier.

The Octagon House is no longer open to the public.

Rienzi Cemetery's first owner was fascinated with spirits

While Rienzi Cemetery is the area's first public cemetery, the ghost stories start before its first burial. Nathaniel Tallmadge, Wisconsin's third territorial governor, buried his son William on the property in 1845 and later donated the first several acres of the official cemetery.

According to archives, Tallmadge was deep in the 19th-century Spiritualist movement, holding seances and documenting ghostly encounters and premonitions. He carried his beliefs with him from New York to Wisconsin and other areas he's called home.

Galloway House & Village supports ghost stories as recently as 2021

Ghost stories surrounding the Galloway House, which finished construction between 1878 and 1880, include hearing clattering plates, children giggling, and various voices throughout the village. A longtime employee in 2007 said she'd never experienced anything paranormal and guessed that rumors had started from children.

However, a one-time public ghost hunt from Caper Company in 2021 reportedly resulted in phenomenon such as recorded voices, drops in temperature and activity on spirit boxes and other equipment.

Visitors outside Capone's report seeing figures in vacant rooms

Capone's, N10302 U.S. 151 in Malone, was built in 1846 as the Stage Coach Inn, but is now known for burgers, pizza and the occasional ghost. Namesake Al Capone is said to have stopped here when traveling between northern Wisconsin and Chicago.

Paranormal activity reported in the business includes pizza pans thrown in the kitchen, a beer glass flying off a counter and the scent of old-fashioned floral perfume wafting through the air. From the outside, visitors and passersby have reported sightings in the third-floor windows, from movement and lights to the figure of a woman.

Halloween is almost here: Know your trick-or-treat times

Most Fond du Lac County communities have yet to hold trick-or-treating, though Ripon held it Oct. 25. The following cities and villages will have trick-or-treating Oct. 31:

  • Fond du Lac: 3:30 to 5:30 p.m.
  • Waupun: 4 p.m. to 6 p.m.
  • North Fond du Lac: 3:30 to 5:30 p.m.
  • Campbellsport: 2 to 4 p.m.
  • Brandon: 4:30 to 6:30 p.m.
  • Eden: 3 to 5 p.m.
  • Oakfield: 3 to 5 p.m.
  • Mt. Calvary: 2 to 4 p.m.
  • Rosendale: 5:30 to 7 p.m.
  • St. Cloud: 3 to 5 p.m.

Daphne Lemke is the Streetwise reporter for the FDL Reporter. Contact her at dlemke@usatodayco.com.
